To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Cr synthesis and ureagenesis are closely linked; (ii) Cr deficiency is associated to OTC and ASS deficiency and HHH syndrome; (iii) Cr levels increase in ASL deficiency, lysinuric-protein intolerance and during arginine loading; (iv) the arginine availability is the main determinant of the plasma Cr levels.

plasma creatine concentrations in urea cycle disorders follow two different trends: they are decreased in OTC, ASS deficiencies and HHS syndrome, whereas they are significantly increased in patients with ASL deficiency and LPI.

plasma creatine levels are decreased in ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC), argininosuccinate synthetase (ASS) deficiencies and hyperornithinaemia, hyperammonaemia, and homocitrullinaemia syndrome (HHH syndrome).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolic pathways involved in Cr synthesis and its relationship with ureagenesis.
the role of arginine availability in the regulation of Cr synthesis in humans, and with the clinical implications of Cr deficiency in UCDs.
the study of the relationships between Cr metabolism and urea cycle defects, with a view to better understanding the role of Cr as a marker of urea cycle function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cr deficiency is not a feature of UCDs.
the Cr pool in patients with UDCs is not only dependent on arginine availability but also on the specific enzyme involved in the UCD.
Cr metabolism is altered in UCDs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in UCDs Cr metabolism is a useful marker of arginine metabolism, and its measurement may be of help in the clinical management of patients with UCD.

the arginine pool in the cell, which is the limiting factor in the urea cycle, is also a limiting factor in the synthesis of creatine, and therefore the measurement of creatine may be a useful tool in the clinical management of urea cycle disorders.
Cr metabolism should be carefully evaluated in UCDs, and that the measurement of plasma Cr concentrations could be a useful tool for the management of these patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the arginine:glycinamide synthetase reaction is the key regulatory step of Cr synthesis in humans.
Cr is a key molecule for both urea cycle and Cr metabolism.
